# Today: Batteries + Boosting

::: {.big-prompt}
Understand the battery. Respect the energy. Follow the order.
:::

Before we work on cars, we need a few basics.

# What is a battery?

::: columns
::: {.column width="46%"}
A battery **stores energy**.

In a car battery, energy is stored chemically.

When the car needs it, the battery releases electrical energy.

::: {.big-prompt}
Stored energy waiting to move.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}

# Energy is transferred

::: columns
::: {.column width="43%"}
Energy is not created or destroyed.

It is **transferred**.

Battery energy can become:

- motion, the starter turns
- heat, wires warm up
- sound, the engine cranks
- light, a spark
:::

# Charge and Discharge

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### CHARGE

<div style="font-size:5rem;text-align:center">⚡ → 🔋</div>

**Energy goes into the battery.**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### DISCHARGE

<div style="font-size:5rem;text-align:center">🔋 → 🚗</div>

**Energy comes out of the battery.**
:::
:::

Think about your phone: plug it in = charge, use it = discharge.

# Voltage and Current

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Voltage = PUSH

<div style="font-size:5rem;text-align:center">➡️ ➡️ ➡️</div>

Voltage helps push electricity through a circuit.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Current = FLOW

<div style="font-size:5rem;text-align:center">••••••••→</div>

Current is how much electrical charge is moving. It is measured in **amps**.
:::
:::

::: {.big-prompt}
Volts push. Amps flow.
:::

# Low Voltage, High Current

<div style="display:flex;gap:2rem;align-items:center;justify-content:center;margin-top:2rem">
  <div style="font-size:6rem;font-weight:800;border:6px solid #3182ce;border-radius:24px;padding:1rem 2rem">12 V</div>
  <div style="font-size:5rem">+</div>
  <div style="font-size:4rem;font-weight:800;border:6px solid #dd6b20;border-radius:24px;padding:1rem 2rem">HIGH AMPS</div>
</div>

A starter needs **a lot of current**. A car battery can deliver hundreds of amps.

A short circuit can create intense heat, sparks, damaged tools, and burns.

# Why are jumper cables thick?

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Thin conductor

<div style="height:18px;background:#c53030;border-radius:10px;margin:4rem 2rem"></div>

Less current capacity. It can heat up faster.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Thick jumper cable

<div style="height:68px;background:#2d3748;border-radius:34px;margin:2.5rem 2rem"></div>

More current needs a **thicker conductor**.
:::
:::

For higher voltage, insulation must be rated to safely contain that voltage.

# DC and AC

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### DC: Direct Current

<svg viewBox="0 0 500 220" role="img" aria-label="Direct current flows in one direction" style="width:100%">
  <line x1="50" y1="110" x2="420" y2="110" stroke="#3182ce" stroke-width="24" stroke-linecap="round"/>
  <polygon points="430,110 380,75 380,145" fill="#3182ce"/>
</svg>

Flows one way. **A battery gives DC.**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### AC: Alternating Current

<svg viewBox="0 0 500 220" role="img" aria-label="Alternating current changes direction repeatedly" style="width:100%">
  <path d="M30,110 C90,20 150,20 210,110 S330,200 390,110 S450,20 480,70" fill="none" stroke="#3182ce" stroke-width="18"/>
</svg>

Changes direction repeatedly. **Wall outlets use AC.**
:::
:::

# Before You Touch the Cables

<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);gap:1.2rem;margin-top:1.5rem;text-align:center">
  <div style="border:4px solid #3182ce;border-radius:18px;padding:1rem"><div style="font-size:4rem">🥽</div><strong>Safety glasses</strong></div>
  <div style="border:4px solid #3182ce;border-radius:18px;padding:1rem"><div style="font-size:4rem">💍</div><strong>Remove loose jewelry</strong></div>
  <div style="border:4px solid #3182ce;border-radius:18px;padding:1rem"><div style="font-size:4rem">🔍</div><strong>Inspect the battery</strong></div>
  <div style="border:4px solid #3182ce;border-radius:18px;padding:1rem"><div style="font-size:4rem">🚫</div><strong>No cracks or leaks</strong></div>
  <div style="border:4px solid #3182ce;border-radius:18px;padding:1rem"><div style="font-size:4rem">🙈</div><strong>Face away</strong></div>
  <div style="border:4px solid #3182ce;border-radius:18px;padding:1rem"><div style="font-size:4rem">✋</div><strong>Teacher permission</strong></div>
</div>

# Boosting Order

<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:1rem;font-size:1.35em">
  <div style="border-left:12px solid #e53e3e;padding:1rem"><strong>1.</strong> RED → dead battery <strong>+</strong></div>
  <div style="border-left:12px solid #e53e3e;padding:1rem"><strong>2.</strong> RED → good battery <strong>+</strong></div>
  <div style="border-left:12px solid #2d3748;padding:1rem"><strong>3.</strong> BLACK → good battery <strong>-</strong></div>
  <div style="border-left:12px solid #2d3748;padding:1rem"><strong>4.</strong> BLACK → solid engine/chassis ground on the dead car, away from the battery</div>
</div>

<div style="font-size:4rem;text-align:center;margin-top:2rem">🔴 → 🔴 → ⚫ → ⚫</div>

# Then What?

1. Check every connection.
2. Start the good vehicle.
3. Try to start the dead vehicle.
4. Once running, remove the cables in **reverse order**.

::: {.big-prompt}
Slow is smooth. Smooth is safe.
:::

# Safe Removal Order

Remove each clamp in reverse order:

1. BLACK from the boosted vehicle's ground.
2. BLACK from the good battery.
3. RED from the good battery.
4. RED from the boosted battery.

Keep every loose clamp under control.

# The Clamp Rule

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
<div style="font-size:7rem;text-align:center">✅</div>

- keep the loose clamp controlled
- move slowly
- keep positive away from metal
- ask before guessing
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
<div style="font-size:7rem;text-align:center">❌</div>

- do not let clamps touch
- do not toss cables around
- do not guess at a connection
:::
:::

# Stop and Call the Teacher

<div style="font-size:9rem;text-align:center">⚠️</div>

Stop if you see **unexpected sparks, smoke, a burning smell, a hot cable, a damaged battery, or anything you are unsure about**.

# Before We Go Outside

1. What does a battery store?
2. Why can a 12 V battery still cause problems?
3. What are the four cable connections, in order?
